public_rationale: For July–September 2024, Microsoft reported roughly 12 percentage points of Azure growth from AI services, while Google reported 35% year-over-year growth in total cloud revenue [e1] [e2]. On October 31, 2024, Amazon described its AI business as a multibillion-dollar annual revenue run rate growing at a triple-digit year-over-year percentage [e3]. These different measures do not establish that any company failed to demonstrate material AI revenue growth [e1] [e2] [e3]. Reuters reported Microsoft down 5.6% intraday on October 31, Amazon up 7% intraday on November 1, and Alphabet up 2.8% on October 30, 2024 [e4] [e5] [e6]. Without establishing the insufficient-growth condition, those reactions do not settle the conditional forecast [e1] [e2] [e3] [e4] [e5] [e6].
limitations: The claim supplies no numerical growth threshold or comparison period.
Azure growth contribution, total cloud revenue and an annualized AI revenue run rate do not provide comparable realized quarterly AI revenue figures [e1] [e2] [e3].
The Microsoft and Amazon market observations are intraday figures [e4] [e5].
The evidence does not connect a demonstrated failure of the revenue condition to the subsequent market reaction.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Microsoft, Amazon and Google will be punished by markets next quarter if they cannot show significant revenue increases from their AI capex.
conditions: if they can't show a significant increase in AI revenue

statement.excerpt: At the beginning of August, Microsoft, Amazon, and Google all took a beating from the markets for their massive capital expenditures related to AI, and all three of them will face the wheel next quarter if they can't show a significant increase in revenue from the combined $150bn (if not more) that they've put into new data centers and NVIDIA GPUs.

from_speaker: all three of them will face the wheel
if they can't show a significant increase in revenue
new data centers and NVIDIA GPUs
our_interpretation: Assess the conditional forecast identified in the normalized proposition. The opening assertion about earlier market losses is background, not a separate forecast.
Read 'next quarter' as the October–December 2024 earnings cycle, including the October announcements and their immediate trading reactions.

Read 'face the wheel' as a substantial adverse share-price reaction associated with disappointing returns from AI investment. Use the first regular trading session after each earnings announcement as the ordinary reaction window.
Read 'significant increase' as a material increase in AI-related revenue demonstrated in the earnings disclosures. Zitron supplies neither a numerical threshold nor a comparison period.
Apply the condition separately to each company. A company showing material AI revenue growth does not test the prediction about what happens without that growth.

The $150 billion describes the claimed investment base, not a revenue target. Evidence need not trace individual revenues to particular GPUs, but total cloud revenue alone does not establish AI revenue.

Use company-reported revenue disclosures to examine the condition. The relevant reporting quarter is July–September 2024, Microsoft's fiscal first quarter and Amazon's and Alphabet's calendar third quarter.
criteria.support_condition: For each company whose disclosures establish that it failed to show material AI revenue growth, a substantial adverse earnings-related market reaction attributable to that shortfall supports the forecast. Supporting the full three-company prediction requires establishing the antecedent and predicted reaction for all three.
criteria.contradiction_condition: At least one company demonstrably fails to show material AI revenue growth yet experiences a clearly favorable or non-punitive earnings reaction. A favorable reaction where the revenue condition did not occur does not contradict the forecast.

evidence.locator: Amy Hood's prepared remarks, Intelligent Cloud results
evidence.explanation: Microsoft disclosed a substantial AI contribution to Azure growth. This measures percentage-point contribution to cloud growth, not a standalone AI revenue series, so it does not establish that the forecast's antecedent occurred.
Google reported strong cloud growth and discussed AI's role in customer adoption. Total cloud revenue includes other services and cannot establish the size or growth of AI revenue alone.

evidence.locator: Andy Jassy's prepared remarks, AWS AI discussion
evidence.publisher: Amazon, transcript reproduced by Stock Analysis
evidence.explanation: In this passage, Jassy described AWS AI as a multibillion-dollar revenue-run-rate business growing at a triple-digit annual percentage. That is material evidence against assuming no demonstrated growth, but it is not a comparable realized quarterly revenue disclosure.

evidence.locator: Opening market report, paragraph beginning 'Shares of Meta'
evidence.explanation: Microsoft experienced a substantial negative reaction, and the report discussed concerns about AI costs and delayed returns. This is an intraday observation; it does not establish failure of the revenue condition.

Amazon's immediate earnings reaction was positive in this intraday report. That would contradict an unconditional sell-off prediction, but the conditional prediction requires evidence that Amazon failed to demonstrate material AI revenue growth.
Alphabet's earnings reaction was positive. Its direction alone cannot contradict the forecast without establishing the revenue antecedent.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable AI revenue disclosures for July–September 2024 and a source-grounded interpretation of significant growth would establish whether the condition occurred for each company. For companies meeting that condition, first-session earnings returns and contemporaneous reporting would establish whether an adverse reaction attributable to the shortfall followed.
